content.introduction: The sources provide information on what an earnings calendar is and how it can be used, but they do not specify any particular earnings reports for today, November 7, 2026. The Investing.com Earnings Calendar describes it as a tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide, displaying EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results. The Zacks Investment Research page explains that an earnings calendar is a schedule of when publicly traded companies report their financial results, typically quarterly, and is a strategic investing tool. The TradingView Earnings Calendar shows the latest and upcoming earnings reports released by companies, allowing customization by time period, country, and time zone. None of these sources provide specific earnings reports for today.
body:
## FAQ

### What is the Investing.com Earnings Calendar?

The Earnings Calendar is a free tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide. It displays EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results once released, so you can compare analyst expectations with reported outcomes in a single view.

### What is an earnings surprise? [...] Most publicly traded companies report earnings four times a year, once per fiscal quarter. Earnings season typically begins a few weeks after each quarter ends, with the busiest reporting periods falling in January, April, July, and October. Not all companies report on the same date, so the Earnings Calendar helps you track which companies are reporting on any given day.

### How do I filter the Earnings Calendar? [...] An earnings surprise occurs when a company's reported EPS or Revenue differs from the analyst consensus forecast. A positive surprise means the company outperformed expectations, while a negative surprise means it underperformed. The Earnings Calendar displays this as the EPS Surprise % and Revenue Surprise % columns, making it easy to spot which companies beat or missed forecasts at a glance.

## What are Earnings?

Earnings refer to a company’s profit, usually measured as earnings per
share (EPS)—the portion of profit allocated to each outstanding share
of stock.

# Calendar

## How to use the Earnings Calendar?

TradingView’s Earnings Calendar shows the latest and upcoming earnings reports released by companies. As an important indicator of a company’s financial state, earnings per share are one of the most followed metrics among traders, so the calendar above can serve as a powerful tool for analysis. [...] With buttons on the upper panel, you can customize the calendar — choose a time period, country, and time zone to see only those reports that suit your strategy. This way, you can decide to see only the earnings of US companies or track reports globally. When all is set, you can easily shift through the calendar to plan your next move.

You can follow companies' earnings in more detail on corresponding symbol pages. Track Tesla's earnings, Amazon's earnings, and even more. [...] All reports are sorted in chronological order, from the oldest ones on top to the newest or future values on the bottom. The calendar is simple but contains all the necessary information — the report’s time and company name, estimated and actual EPS, surprise, and the company’s market capitalization. Clicking on any of the financial metrics will sort the report in the table.
